title: DNA Structure: Evidence and Credit
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。出版社の解答ページは未提供です。

passages.text:
In 1953, three consecutive papers in Nature presented a model and X-ray evidence concerning the structure of DNA. The best-known paper, by James Watson and Francis Crick, proposed two chains winding around a common axis, with bases paired inside and sugar-phosphate backbones outside. The model was not a direct photograph of individual atoms. It was an argument constrained by chemistry, molecular dimensions, base composition, and diffraction data.

Different researchers supplied different constraints. Erwin Chargaff's measurements showed regularities in base ratios. Rosalind Franklin and Raymond Gosling produced high-quality X-ray diffraction patterns and quantitative structural information; Maurice Wilkins, Alec Stokes, and Herbert Wilson also reported X-ray results. Model building then tested whether a three-dimensional arrangement could satisfy these observations without impossible bonds or distances.

The paired structure suggested a mechanism for copying: if each base pairs specifically with its complement, either strand can guide formation of a partner. “Suggested” matters. A plausible implication of a structure is not yet a demonstrated cellular mechanism. Later experiments, including work on semiconservative replication, supplied additional evidence. Scientific knowledge grew through a sequence of model, prediction, and test.

The history also raises questions about access and credit. Data can contribute to a correct model while the conditions under which they were seen or communicated remain ethically contested. Recognition should therefore follow more than the final publication's author line. It should identify who produced data, developed methods, interpreted evidence, built models, and tested consequences. Correct science does not make questions of consent, attribution, or institutional power disappear.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: The DNA structure was obtained from a direct photograph and required no later testing.

options.label: B
options.text: The DNA model combined multiple kinds of evidence, generated testable implications, and raises questions about access and credit.

options.label: C
options.text: Only the final paper's author list matters when assigning scientific recognition.

options.label: D
options.text: Ethical concerns determine whether a molecular model is chemically correct.

questions.answer: 正解：B。本文は複数の制約からのモデル構築、複製予測の後続検証、データへのアクセスと貢献認定を統合しています。A・C・Dは証拠、検証、科学的妥当性と倫理の関係を誤ります。

questions.prompt: Which set lists four types of evidence or constraints used to evaluate DNA models?

options.label: A
options.text: Chemical bonding, molecular dimensions, base composition, and X-ray diffraction patterns

options.label: B
options.text: Publication order, laboratory size, newspaper coverage, and researcher age

options.label: C
options.text: Consent rules, institutional rank, model popularity, and citation count

options.label: D
options.text: Direct atomic photographs, clinical trials, fossil evidence, and weather records

questions.answer: 正解：A。化学結合、分子寸法、塩基組成・比率、X線回折が構造候補を制約しました。B・Cは社会的要因、Dは本文にない証拠を混ぜています。

questions.prompt: The word “constraint” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: a condition that rules out structures that cannot satisfy it

options.label: B
options.text: an untested personal preference with no evidential role

options.label: C
options.text: a guarantee that only one researcher can build a model

options.label: D
options.text: a photograph showing every atom directly

questions.answer: 正解：A。constraintは不可能な結合や距離などを持つ構造を排除する条件です。Bは証拠性を否定し、C・Dは本文のモデル構築と回折データの性質を誤ります。

questions.prompt: Why does the passage emphasize that X-ray diffraction was not a direct photograph of individual atoms?

options.label: A
options.text: Researchers had to infer a structure by combining diffraction patterns with chemical, dimensional, and compositional constraints.

options.label: B
options.text: The patterns contained no information relevant to molecular structure.

options.label: C
options.text: The model could ignore bond lengths and base ratios.

options.label: D
options.text: Diffraction automatically displayed the complete double helix without interpretation.

questions.answer: 正解：A。回折像は解釈を要する証拠であり、化学・寸法・塩基組成などと組み合わせて構造を推論しました。B～Dは回折情報の価値または解釈の必要性を否定します。

questions.prompt: What distinction does the author make by saying that the paired structure “suggested” a copying mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: A structural implication was plausible, but later experiments were needed to demonstrate how replication occurs in cells.

options.label: B
options.text: The structure proved every detail of cellular replication immediately.

options.label: C
options.text: Complementary pairing had no possible connection to copying.

options.label: D
options.text: Predictions and tests are unnecessary once a model is published.

questions.answer: 正解：A。相補的塩基対は複製機構を予測させましたが、細胞内機構の実証には半保存的複製などの後続実験が必要でした。B～Dは示唆と実証を混同します。

questions.prompt: Which statement best reflects the passage's treatment of scientific validity and research ethics?

options.label: A
options.text: A model can be scientifically correct while questions about consent, data access, attribution, and institutional power remain unresolved.

options.label: B
options.text: Ethically contested data automatically make every scientific conclusion false.

options.label: C
options.text: A correct result eliminates the need to examine how evidence was obtained or credited.

options.label: D
options.text: Ethical conduct alone proves that a molecular structure is chemically possible.

questions.answer: 正解：A。本文はモデルの科学的正しさと、同意・アクセス・帰属・制度的権力の倫理問題を区別しつつ両方を評価します。B～Dはいずれか一方を他方の十分条件にしています。

questions.prompt: According to the passage, which contributions should recognition identify?

options.label: A
options.text: Producing data, developing methods, interpreting evidence, building models, and testing consequences

options.label: B
options.text: Only appearing first on the best-known publication

options.label: C
options.text: Only directing the institution in which the work occurred

options.label: D
options.text: Only proposing a model, regardless of evidence or later tests

questions.answer: 正解：A。最終論文の著者欄だけでなく、データ生成、方法開発、証拠解釈、モデル構築、帰結の検証を認定すべきだと述べています。B～Dは貢献の一部だけに限定します。

questions.prompt: What does the word “argument” mean in the final sentence of paragraph 1?

options.label: A
options.text: a reasoned inference supported and limited by several kinds of evidence

options.label: B
options.text: a personal quarrel between researchers

options.label: C
options.text: a direct image requiring no interpretation

options.label: D
options.text: a claim unconstrained by measurements or chemistry

questions.answer: 正解：A。ここでargumentは口論ではなく、複数の証拠に支えられ制約された推論です。Bは日常語義への誤誘導、C・Dは本文の直接写真ではない点と制約を否定します。

questions.prompt: Which collaboration policy best addresses the passage's concerns about access and credit?

options.label: A
options.text: Record permissions, preserve data provenance and versions, define contribution roles, and provide independent review of attribution disputes.

options.label: B
options.text: Allow unrestricted data access and assign all credit only to the final model builders.

options.label: C
options.text: Delete records of who produced data once a model is accepted.

options.label: D
options.text: Let institutional rank determine consent, access, and authorship without review.

questions.answer: 正解：A。許可、来歴・版管理、役割記録、独立した異議審査は同意・アクセス・帰属・権力の問題に直接対応します。B～Dは出所と貢献を消し、権力の偏りを固定します。
